recentItems.title: Robert Pattinson and cast of 'Primetime' arrive in Venice
recentItems.description:
(5 Sep 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Venice, Italy - 5 September 2026
1. Various of Robert Pattinson arriving and meeting fans 
2. Medium of Merritt Wever arriving 
3. Various of Skyler Gisondo arriving and posing for photographs
4. Mid of Bokeem Woodbine arriving and posing for photographs
5. Various of Phoebe Bridgers arriving 
6. Various of director Lance Oppenheim arriving and posing for photographs 


STORYLINE:
Robert Pattinson sailed into Venice on Saturday alongside his castmates and the director of their latest film, "Primetime." 

The drama will have its world premiere at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival later on Saturday.

Pattinson stars in the film as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen.

"Ren Fare" documentary-maker Lance Oppenheim makes his narrative feature debut with the thriller, which he developed with Pattinson.

The film follows real-life TV star and journalist Hansen as he presents his show "To Catch a Predator" - in which he set out to catch child predators via elaborate sting operations.

It also stars Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, Phoebe Bridgers, Matthew Maher and Bokeem Woodbine.

recentItems.title: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing meets with Vietnamese leaders in Hanoi
recentItems.description:
(5 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS  
Hanoi, Vietnam - 5 September 2026
1. Various of Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing and Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung shaking hands
2. Close of Ho Chi Minh's bust
3. Various of meeting between Min Aung Hlaing and Le Minh Hung 
4. Min Aung Hlaing and Chairman of National Assembly  of Vietnam Tran Thanh Man shaking hands
5. Various of meeting between Min Aung Hlaing and Tran Thanh Man
STORYLINE:
Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing met with Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung and Chairman of the National Assembly Tran Thanh Man on Saturday as he continues his official visit to Hanoi to strengthen ties with the fellow Southeast Asian country. 

Min Aung Hlaing arrived in Vietnam on Friday, his latest diplomatic engagement as he seeks to normalize relations with other Southeast Asian countries and restore Myanmar’s standing within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

He has stepped up diplomatic engagements since being sworn in as president in April following an election that critics say was designed to cement the military’s hold on power.

The outreach is part of an attempt to rebuild regional ties that deteriorated after Min Aung Hlaing ousted Aung San Suu Kyi’s government in February 2021 while serving as army chief.

The visit marks Min Aung Hlaing’s third trip to an ASEAN member state as he seeks to restore his standing within the 11-member bloc.

He was barred from top-level ASEAN meetings for failing to comply with a peace plan for Myanmar adopted by the bloc in April 2021.

Vietnam has maintained longstanding military ties with Myanmar, including defense cooperation and the involvement of Viettel, Vietnam’s military-run telecommunications group, in Mytel, one of Myanmar’s major telecom operators.

Economic ties, however, have weakened, with bilateral trade falling from $853 million in 2020 to $590 million in 2025 and $335 million in the first half of 2026, according to figures Min Aung Hlaing shared with Vietnam’s foreign minister during a meeting in Myanmar in late August.

Western governments have shunned and sanctioned Min Aung Hlaing and his associates for overthrowing Suu Kyi’s government and for serious human rights violations committed since.

The military’s deadly crackdown on protests helped trigger a nationwide armed resistance movement and a bloody civil war.

AP video shot by Hau Dinh

recentItems.title: Lebanon says 3, including a child, killed in Israeli strikes in the south and in Bekaa Valley
recentItems.description:
(5 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS   
Mayfadoun, Lebanon - 5 September 2026
1. Various of rubble and destroyed homes at scene of strike
2. Men walking through rubble
3. Mid of Jamal Salameh checking his destroyed home
4. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Jamal Salameh, father of Mariam, who was killed in a strike in Mayfadoun:
“We were sitting here peacefully, and I was supposed to enroll my daughter in high school. We were sitting out here in the evening and all of a sudden a missile hit. We lost consciousness. What were they targeting? What did they think I had here? As you can see, there’s nothing. These were kids, what did they do wrong?”
5. Backpack filled with books among rubble
6. Man inspecting destroyed car
7. Men standing among rubble
8. Man walking past rubble and destroyed car
9. Various of rubble and destroyed homes at scene of strike
STORYLINE:
Lebanon’s health ministry said three people were killed and 23 wounded in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon and the eastern Bekaa Valley on Friday.

In the town of Mayfadoun, residents walked through the rubble and searched for belongings among the destroyed homes.

Jamal Salameh tearfully walked through the remains of his home, remembering his daughter Mariam, who was due to start high school in the coming days.

“We were sitting out here in the evening and all of a sudden a missile hit. We lost consciousness. What were they targeting? What did they think I had here? As you can see, there’s nothing,” Salameh said. “These were kids, what did they do wrong?”

The Israeli military said in a statement that it had carried out the strikes in response to a drone fired by Hezbollah at Israeli forces in southern Lebanon. The drone was shot down and no soldiers were injured, it said.

recentItems.title: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte posts bail after arrest for alleged threats against Marcos
recentItems.description:
(5 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS  
Quezon city, NCR, Philippines - 5 September 2026
1. Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte exiting courtroom
2. Duterte showing document of court order to camera
3. SOUNDBITE (Tagalog) Sara Duterte, Philippines Vice President: 
“'Our (lawyers') advice to you is to get bail because our countrymen will be able to protect you if you are outside and free. Instead of surrendering to the police where they will hide you and our countrymen will not know what will happen to you inside.' 
 That was the advice of my lawyers.”
4. Wide of Duterte talking to media 
5. SOUNDBITE (Tagalog) Sara Duterte, Philippines Vice President: 
“What does this administration really want to do with me? My request to you, like what we did earlier, there should be someone in front of me and someone at the back so that I can go down and ride my vehicle. Can I ask you a favor?"
6. Various of Duterte exiting court building 
7. Wide of Duterte lawyer Atty Paul Lawrence Lim talking to journalist 
8. SOUNDBITE (English/Tagalog) Atty Paul Lawrence Lim, lawyer of Duterte: 
“She (Duterte) was processed, she voluntarily appeared again without prejudice to her pending question on the issue of jurisdiction. She voluntarily appeared to the court that issued the warrant so that it maybe lifted. So she went to the same process as all accuses, no special treatment, she submitted all the requirements and she posted bail.”  
9. Wide of police and journalists outside court building 
STORYLINE:
Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail on Saturday after an order was issued for her arrest the previous day on charges that she publicly threatened to arrange the assassination of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and two other people. 

Emerging from Quezon City Regional Trial Court in Metro Manila in a black outfit, Duterte consoled her supporters, hugging a woman who was sobbing as supporters chanted “Duterte! Duterte!”

The vice president showed a court order lifting the arrest warrant issued by the court Friday and said her lawyers instructed her to keep a copy on hand. 

She urged journalists to surround her on the way to her car because she did not feel safe. 

"My request to you, like what we did earlier, there should be someone in front of me and someone at the back so that I can go down and ride my vehicle. Can I ask you a favor?"

Paul Lawrence Lim, one of her attorneys, said court staff took Duterte’s fingerprints and she posted 360,000 pesos bail ($5,740) for three counts of grave threats. 

After the arrest order was issued on Friday, he said Duterte would fight the charges.

“She voluntarily appeared to the court that issued the warrant so that it maybe lifted," Lim told the press.

"She went to the same process as all accuses, no special treatment, she submitted all the requirements and she posted bail.”  

Duterte was impeached by the House of Representatives in May on the threat charges, as well as alleged financial anomalies. 

She has denied the allegations.

The case is seen as part of a high-stakes political showdown pitting Duterte against Marcos. 

A conviction may permanently disqualify her from holding public office and prohibit her from seeking the presidency in 2028, when Marcos's six-year term ends.

The charges stem from an alleged threat Duterte, 48, made during a 2024 online news conference. 

She said she would have Marcos, his wife and then-House of Representatives Speaker Martin Romualdez killed by an assassin if she herself was killed as their political disputes escalated.

recentItems.title: In Congo’s Ebola epicenter, a burial team works under threats and a ticking clock
recentItems.description:
(5 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Rwankole, the Democratic Republic of the Congo – 4 September 2026
1. Wide of burial team putting on protective clothing ahead of burial of Ebola victim
2. Mid of burial team members disinfecting clothing 
3. Mid of burial team member putting on gloves 
4. SOUNDBITE (French) Benjamin Muhindo, member of Dignified and Safe Burial team:
“Burials during this Ebola outbreak are very complicated. We're racing against time, and there are many deaths, so many people are dying.”
5. Various of burial team preparing body in secured room
6. Mid of relatives of deceased watching from outside room
7. Burial team members placing body in coffin
8. SOUNDBITE (French) Benjamin Muhindo, member of the Dignified and Safe Burial team:
“The main goal is to protect the community, and we try to reassure people when there are threats. We try to calm the situation because our team includes a communications officer who will talk with the community to help them understand that we are in the midst of an epidemic.”
9. Burial team members carrying coffin to truck
10. Truck carrying bodies leaving Ebola treatment center for cemetery
11. Burial team members and relatives at cemetery
12. SOUNDBITE (French) Adolphe Yuma Tumba, member of the Dignified and Safe Burial team:
“Most of the time we face threats and most of the time these threats are verbal. It also happens often that they are physical, but less so because, as time goes on, people are beginning to understand what this is all about.”
13. Various of burial team members carrying coffin and lowering into grave
14. Various of relatives crying
15. SOUNDBITE (Swahili) Sofia Wanito, mother of Ebola victim:
“Honestly, we older women just don't understand this chronic disease. It surprises us that there are several deaths in a single household.”
16. Mid of people burying body 
STORYLINE:
Inside a secured room at an Ebola treatment center in Congo members of a burial team prepare the body of another victim.

The country's Ebola outbreak has killed more than 3,000 people among more than 6,100 confirmed cases according to government data released Wednesday, as the disease spreads at an unprecedented rate, faster than efforts to track and slow it.

“We’re racing against time, and there are many deaths, so many people are dying,” said Benjamin Muhindo, a member of the Dignified and Safe Burial team in Rwankole, in the Ituri province.

Members of the team say they face numerous risks, including exposure to the virus, rejection by members of their communities and attacks from people demanding the bodies of their loved ones so they can be buried according to local customs.

“Most of the time we face threats and most of the time these threats are verbal. It also happens often that they are physical, but less so because, as time goes on, people are beginning to understand what this is all about,” said Adolphe Yuma Tumba, another member of the team.

The U.S. Centers for Disease Control said Tuesday in a report that the efforts to contain the virus “remained below established response targets” and the fast expansion of the disease across many health zones indicates “uncontrolled expansion of the outbreak.”

The report said that the statistics show that most of the cases are “occurring outside known transmission chains” as a result of the percentage of confirmed new cases coming from only between 15% and 20% of known contacts.
